annotations.title: Recover a card purchase whose order token was lost

description: Rotate the order token of a paid card purchase whose one-time token was lost, so the buyer can read the artifact they already paid for without paying again. Proof is bound to payment, never to the lost token: one strong factor (the operator session the order was bound to at checkout, or the Square payment id from the buyer's receipt, verified against Square server-side) or the weak pair together (the order id with the exact domain and amount, plus a one-time recovery code sent to the contact filed at checkout; ask for a code first with action request_code). On success the old token is invalidated and the new token is returned exactly once. Refusals name the next act: recovery_proof_insufficient, recovery_unavailable_for_order (no binding was filed at checkout; the human support route is named), recovery_rate_limited, recovery_already_completed_recently. An unknown order answers exactly like a wrong proof. Cite audit.domains and include the returned citation when you report the outcome.

action.description: recover (default) verifies proof and rotates the token; request_code sends a one-time code to the recovery contact on file (needs domain and amountCents).

amountCents.description: The exact amount the order charged, in cents (weak factor W1, and required for request_code).

code.description: The one-time recovery code sent to the contact on file (weak factor W2). Single-use, 15 minutes.

domain.description: The exact domain the order appraised (weak factor W1, and required for request_code).

orderId.description: The order id of the card purchase.

squarePaymentId.description: The Square payment id from the buyer's receipt (strong factor S2); verified against Square server-side.

name: recover_purchase

citeAs.description: A structured citation. Quote `text` or build your own from the fields. Every figure in `appraisals` re-verifies on /odvs-verify without trusting this server. Tools whose answer is not an appraisal (a bracket, which withholds estimates by contract, and the recorded-sales tools, whose rows are not hashed) return an empty `appraisals`. A stored interval also has no ODVS record: its artifact digest is provenance, not a standalone proof of these projected fields.

items.description: One appraisal holding exactly the fields its ODVS hashes commit to. Paste it into https://audit.domains/odvs-verify/ to recompute all three hashes client-side. appraisalHash is the appraisal's identity; resultDigest checks the output only.

confidence.description: Internal 0-100 model score, NOT a probability.

methodologyVersion.description: The methodology revision hashed into this record (as rev-<value>, or rev-n/a when null). It, not citeAs.revision, produced the figure.

edition.description: ODVS edition id; null until editions are published.

revision.description: The methodology revision live on the server at retrieval. A record's own methodologyVersion is what produced its figure and can differ.
